newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - June 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng will lead the Chinese delegation that will attend Hong Kong's handover ceremony on the evening of June 30. British Prime Minister Tony Blair plans to attend the ceremony but not the swearing-in of the post-handover provisional legislature.

-- Research shows more than 90 percent of people in the southern Chinese cities of Guangzhou and Shenzhen want to watch Hong Kong's handover ceremony, while 60 percent would like to come to the territory to witness the event.
-- SING TAO -- An eight-month inquiry concluded the Hong Kong government was justified in forcing former immigration chief Laurence Leung into early retirement.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- China Light & Power will lay off another 1,000 people after it merges two departments. Union leaders said some workers laid off in March still had not found new jobs.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- The mayor of Shenzhen, Li Zebin, said Hong Kong and the southern Chinese city would become sister cities and would prosper together. He said the Hong Kong handover would provide valuable development opportunities for Shenzhen.

-- WEN WEI PO -- The chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Committee, Li Ruihuan, told reporters in Germany that western countries did not fully understand China's attitude towards human rights issues.

-- Gifts for the post-handover government have started to arrive in Hong Kong from all corners of the mainland. A jade sculpture titled "A Smooth Journey" has arrived from Guangdong province, while others in bronze, steel and shell are on their way.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Industry sources said Beijing authorities had forced three Shanghai-based financial institutions to replace senior executives after they participated in irregular share practices.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A U.S. Congressional delegation attending the handover ceremony planned to join Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in boycotting the swearing-in ceremony of the provisional legislature.
